Fortune Procurement System is the company's online system for the entire purchasing

from the moment someone needs something, through finding a supplier, placing a formal order, and checking in what arrives. It replaces printed forms, phone calls, and email chains with one place where everyone can see exactly where a request stands.

Every person who uses the system sees a different set of screens depending on their role: Employee, Planning, Warehouse, Procurement, Approver (Supervisor, Department Head, Operations Manager, Director, or Finance Director), Supplier, TSQA (Quality Assurance), or Admin. This manual is organized by what you can do in the system, and each section notes which role(s) can use that feature. If a feature described here doesn't appear on your screen, your role or position may not have access to it â€” check with your Admin.

Creating a Raw Material or Service Request Directly (PR2)

Planning staff request raw materials or certain services directly, skipping the PR1 step and warehouse stock check, since Planning's requests are based on their own production forecasting rather than checking existing stock.
Planning Staff: click "PR2" (or "New Request") in the left sidebar.
Choose a Purpose, Date Required, and Priority.
Add line items: description, unit of measure, and quantity.
Click Save Draft or Submit. A submitted request goes straight into internal certification it does not go through Warehouse.
Tips and things to watch out for
Only users in the Planning Staff position can create a PR2 this way; other Employees must use PR1.

Your "My Requests" list shows the full downstream journey of each request you created not just its internal approval status, but whether a Purchase Order has been sent, a delivery is in progress, or the goods receipt is complete.

Your Approval Queue only ever shows items sitting at your own

Some approval steps only apply above or below a certain purchase amount â€” if a request doesn't meet that threshold, that step is skipped automatically and won't appear in your queue.

Receiving Goods and Closing the Goods Receipt (GRN)
Warehouse (goods and raw materials) or Procurement (services)
Warehouse (for goods and raw materials) or Procurement (for services) record what
against a Purchase Order, and formally close out the order once everything is checked.
Warehouse or Procurement: click "Goods Receipt" (GRN) in the left sidebar.
Open the relevant Purchase Order's receiving record.
For each line, enter the quantity
. Note any discrepancy, and any rejected quantity with a reason.
Optionally flag any goods line as "Forward to QA" if you want it inspected.
Click Save Progress to keep the GRN Open for further receiving passes, or Close GRN once everything including QA is resolved.

Tips and things to watch out for
Every Raw Material line is automatically and mandatorily flagged for QA â€” this can't be turned off.
If anything is still pending QA, the GRN status becomes "Pending QA
and it cannot be closed until TSQA resolves it.
A closed GRN can be reopened later by Warehouse or Procurement if a correction is needed.
For services requiring compliance documentation, receiving can't be finalized until that document is uploaded.
TSQA inspect and sign off on raw materials and any goods flagged for quality checking before they can count as received.
TSQA: click "QA Queue" in the left sidebar.

You can reverse a decision (Approve after a Reject, or the reverse)
the GRN is still open once it's closed, QA decisions are locked permanently.
There is no supplier-facing "resubmit after rejection" flow â€” a rejected raw material stays blocked until you personally change the decision to Approved.
